assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin therapies is a clear, specific discovery chain (proglucagon processing, incretin action, stable agonists) that has changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and opened cardiometabolic and possibly neurological indications. Impact on the field and on patients is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1) and Drucker (biology of GLP-1 and GLP-2 and clinical translation) are central. Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is credible but contested in the public record; Knudsen's work on long-acting agonists is largely industrial development and fits less naturally in a three-person prize. Habener and Bell are not on the supplied list, so the configuration cannot be complete.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of confirmation and large outcome trials; recognition appears timely and increasingly pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for the active peptide identification is disputed and I cannot resolve it from the supplied text.
Whether the prize should reward basic physiology, drug design or both is open.
Long-term safety and effects beyond weight and glucose are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave the field causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and is a methodological invention with enormous, durable influence across neuroscience and now early therapeutic use. The core discovery of channelrhodopsins and their use as neuronal tools is clear.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier conceptual work (Miesenbock) are all real contributions. With a three-person limit the selection is difficult and some contributors will be left out; my choice favors the molecular discovery plus the leading demonstration in mammalian neurons.
assessment.maturity: Roughly twenty years of broad independent adoption; the method is mature, and clinical vision restoration adds support.
uncertainties: Credit split between the discovery of the tool and its first neuronal application is contested.
Physiology or Medicine versus Chemistry framing is uncertain.
I am relying on memory for the exact chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic class, a clear discovery-to-medicine story with a clear shift in oncology practice.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T with costimulation), Sadelain (second-generation CAR design and preclinical work) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells) cover the main arcs; others, such as Eshhar, Zelig and Kuwana, are not credited here, so the configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and long-term follow-up exist; solid-tumor results and toxicity remain limiting, but the core finding is established.
uncertainties: Missing early inventors on the supplied list weaken a fair prize configuration.
Durability and cure rates are still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines are a rare case of a basic virology discovery producing population-level prevention of a cancer, with demonstrated falls in infection and cervical precancer. The impact is lasting and well documented.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly) and Frazer (VLP vaccine development) are the plausible trio; the zur Hausen recognition in 2008 covered the causal virus link, so the VLP step is separate. Others, such as Zhou, may deserve credit, and I cannot assess that from the list.
assessment.maturity: Clinical effectiveness is well confirmed in many countries; cancer-incidence data are now accumulating, so timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over the VLP technology and the role of Zhou are unresolved here.
Overlap with an earlier HPV prize may be viewed as reducing novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new organelle-to-nucleus signaling logic, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, and ATF6 and PERK arms, and now matters to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is fundamental, original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the decisive contributors with a natural two-person configuration; Ron's work on PERK and the integrated stress response is not on the list, so the broader field is not fully captured.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation across species; mechanisms are well established, and therapeutic translation is still early.
uncertainties: Whether the clinical relevance is strong enough for medicine rather than chemistry or biology is open.
Missing credit for related branches such as PERK.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition by imatinib is the proof-of-principle for targeted cancer therapy, transforming CML from fatal to chronic. Importance and clarity are very high, though much of the underlying biology (the Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL, kinases) has been recognized previously in other contexts.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound discovery) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are the natural trio; Rowley and Witte are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of clinical evidence and widespread use; maturity is very high, which if anything suggests the opening for recognition is long-standing.
uncertainties: Industrial versus academic credit; possible concern that the field may have been under-weighted historically.
Whether the foundational oncogene discoveries make the prize a compound recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The separation of lymphocytes into T and B lineages, with distinct thymic and bursal or bone marrow origins, is foundational to modern immunology and underpins immunotherapy and vaccines. The discovery is original, clear and a lasting framework.
assessment.attribution: Miller (thymus function and T cells) and Cooper (B-cell lineage and class switching) are the evident pair, supported by the historical record of Glick's bursa work not being on the list.
assessment.maturity: Mature and canonical, but recognition would be late; the main concern is timeliness for living laureates.
uncertainties: The role of Glick and others in the bursal findings is not captured.
Historic discoveries may sit better with older honors than a current prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of TOR and the mTOR pathway as the master regulator of growth in response to nutrients is a deep, original and widely validated insight with implications for cancer, metabolism, aging and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall (TOR discovery in yeast and its function) is decisive; Sabatini (mTOR identification in mammals and nutrient-sensing) is also central, but Sabatini's credit is complicated by recent controversies, and Brown and Schreiber's work on rapamycin target identification and Heitman are not captured the same way. I propose a Hall-led pair with that caveat.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many labs for three decades; the clinical translation (rapalogs) is real but modest compared with the basic impact.
uncertainties: Credit for mammalian mTOR identification is shared among several groups.
Attribution complicated by non-scientific considerations around one candidate, which I cannot assess.
